messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — I'm carving the dedicated-capacity roadmap into smaller feature slices for the next sprint. We have a backlog of customer asks (carryover, quota visibility, per-tenant autoscale policies) + infra debt (fairness allocator, telemetry). Need to decide priorities by EOD.
Maria Gomez: +1 on slicing. Can we list the customer-impacting items first? Lara has a critical ask from Acme about predictable burst credit behavior. :eyes:
Lara Kim: Acme CS here — they want: 1) clear burst credit expiration rules, 2) per-tenant spike protection to avoid noisy neighbors, 3) a soft-fallback model when reserved pool is exhausted. They need answers for contract handoff next week.
Priya Nair: Noted. For spike protection, we've got two options: preemptive shaping (throttles at admission) or reactive eviction (drain lower-priority sessions). Preemptive is friendlier for customers but harder to tune.
Samir Patel: Reactive eviction is simpler to implement quickly. We can pair it with a queue and eviction score. But it has worse UX under sharp bursts.
Joel Rivera: From infra side — fairness allocator (we called it "ledger-based shaper") is ~3w of work. Telemetry for per-tenant p95/p99 token cost is another 1w. Both are useful for long-term SLOs.
Alex Chen: Proposal: split into 3 slices this sprint: A) Burst behavior policy & short-term fallback (customer-facing), B) Autoscale hysteresis + per-tenant caps (ops-facing), C) Observability + billing signals (telemetry). Prioritise A > B > C. Thoughts?
Maria Gomez: A makes sense for Acme. But C is important for billing and disputes — we should fast-follow. Could we do a tiny telemetry shim in A? e.g., emit "burst-event" tags to existing logs.
Priya Nair: Agree on shim. Also need a clear launch checklist for A. Suggest: acceptance criteria: 1) deterministic burst-credit expiry, 2) soft-fallback routes to shared-model with < 2s extra latency 95% of time, 3) ops runbook for manual override.
Alex Chen: Good. Draft acceptance checklist: - feature flag gated; - e2e test simulating 3x normal burst and ensuring fallback triggers; - customer-facing doc explaining behavior; - metrics: fallback-rate, 95th extra-latency after fallback.
Samir Patel: Quick config prototype I sketched for the fallback policy:
```
fallback_policy:
  enabled: true
  trigger_condition: "reserved_pool_utilization >= 95% or queue_wait > 500ms"
  fallback_target: "hosted-compatible-variant"
  max_extra_latency_ms: 2000
```
Priya Nair: Nice. We should also include a per-tenant admission cap parameter to avoid one tenant burning all burst credits: `tenant_max_burst_ratio: 0.25` (25% of pool).
Maria Gomez: Question on billing: when a tenant hits fallback and routes to shared model, do we bill them at reserved price or shared price? Lara, what does Acme expect?
Lara Kim: Acme: they expect reserved price unless fallback used intentionally by us. They want a buffer/notice and then fallback costs at shared rate with a notification webhook.
Alex Chen: Ok policy: fallback -> bill at shared rate, but provide webhook + 5m grace notice (if possible). Capture acceptance as part of A.
Joel Rivera: On autoscale hysteresis (slice B) — we need to decide on time windows. Current idea: scale-up when sustained > 70% utilization for 90s; scale-down after utilization < 50% for 5m. That prevents thrash.
Samir Patel: Add another guard: limit scale-down steps to 1 instance per cooldown window. Also add a `preempt_weight` for reserved customers vs best-effort.
Priya Nair: We should run a small simulation using last 30 days of traffic to estimate p95 tail impact for chosen windows. Ops can provide traces.
Alex Chen: Action items summary: - Samir/Joe (Joel) implement fallback shim + config prototype for A (owner: Samir) - Priya to run simulation for autoscale windows (owner: Priya) - Maria/Lara to draft customer-facing fallback doc and webhook wording (owner: Maria) - Samir to add `burst-event` telemetry tags in the same PR (owner: Samir)
Maria Gomez: Timeline: aiming for an internal canary by mid-sprint and customer pilot with Acme by week after next. :thumbsup:
Lara Kim: Acme is ok with a pilot; they'll want weekly sync and a short test plan. I'll schedule.
Priya Nair: Quick poll — for prioritization sprint we lock scope to only A + small telemetry shim, move B to next sprint unless simulation shows urgent regressions. React with :one: for lock A-only, :two: for include B as well.
deply-bot: poll created (1: lock A-only, 2: include B).
Alex Chen: Vote: :one:
Samir Patel: Vote: :one:
Maria Gomez: Vote: :one:
Joel Rivera: Vote: :two: (leaning to include B if small ops effort)
Lara Kim: :one:
Alex Chen: Looks like A-only wins. We'll keep B as a stretch goal if Priya's sim shows small impact. Final note: include an item in the sprint retro to capture customer communication clarity — we tripped on ambiguous fallback billing before.
Priya Nair: I'll upload simulation outline to the ticket and tag this thread.
Samir Patel: Starting branch now, will add config and simple tests.
Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10am to check progress.
deploy-bot: reminder: next deploy freeze Thu 22:00 UTC — plan accordingly.
